en: The Sūtra on the King Adorned with All Meritorious Virtues, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing by Imperial Decree during the Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying in the city of Rājagṛha at the Kalandaka [Nivāsa].
In the Bamboo Grove Garden by the pond,
he was together with a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus and twelve hundred bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
They all attained dhāraṇīs and eloquence without obstruction;
they acquired undefiled wisdom and roamed in the realm of non-obstruction,
employing skillful means and expedients to gather and guide sentient beings.
Observing the world,
his mental conduct was impartial;
his intention to benefit others through compassion was pure.
They were able to inquire about the profoundly subtle and wondrous Dharma from all the Buddhas.
Their names were the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Nityodyukta.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samatāvihārin,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāmati,
and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Anantapratibhāna.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vīramati,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vimatisamudghātin.
These and other great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas served as the leaders, together with the Śakras,
Brahmās, World-Protectors, the Four Heavenly Kings, the nāgas, spirits, and the eight classes of beings,
as well as six thousand followers of non-Buddhist paths.
Each leading their own retinues, they all gathered like clouds;
this great assembly all arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and circumambulated him three times to the right.
Rain fell from the heavens of exquisite celestial flowers, and celestial music was played;
various famous incenses were burned as offerings.
At that time, the great assembly all spoke these words:
“Excellent, excellent! The teaching of the Tathāgata possesses great majesty and power;
those who take refuge and have faith in it are able to sever their afflictions.
Having spoken these words, they each sat to one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered the samādhi called "Severing Delusions and Departing from Defilement.
As he entered this meditative absorption, the great earth immediately shook in six ways,
and a rain of fine, subtle sandalwood powder fell from the sky.
Furthermore, exquisite celestial flowers were spread everywhere,
emitting great radiance that pervaded the entire world.
Any sentient beings who had fallen into the evil realms were liberated upon being touched by this light.
It likewise reached all the abodes of the eight classes of beings— devas, nāgas, yakṣas,
and so forth— so that their palaces were all clearly illuminated;
they heard celestial music and the exquisite fragrance of the heavens.
When those devas witnessed this inconceivable and rare event,
they all had this thought: "Who has performed such supreme supernatural power as to cause the earth to tremble greatly and rain down celestial fragrant flowers?"
They emitted great radiance that illuminated the palace.
Having formed this thought, they said to one another,
"This is the Tathāgata manifesting his great majestic power."
"No other gods or beings are capable of such an auspicious omen as this.
We should now go to the Bamboo Grove,
approach the World-Honored One, pay him homage, make offerings, and listen to the sublime Dharma."
Each of them held large *utpala* flowers, *kubjaka* flowers, *puṇḍarīka* flowers, *sugandhika* flowers,
*māndārava* flowers, and *mahāmāndārava* flowers.
They went to where the World-Honored One was, prostrated at his feet,
and made offerings by raining down a multitude of celestial flowers,
which filled the earth until they reached up to the knees.
Beholding the Honored One’s countenance with palms joined in reverence, there were also immeasurable bodhisattvas from other directions,
as well as the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Maṇivikrīḍita-rāja,
and ten billion devas, mantra-holding spirit-kings, and divine protectors.
Beholding the great radiance, each by their own majestic power,
creating exquisite adornments of incense, flowers, and music,
they came to where the Buddha was.
Together with their retinues, they all circumambulated [the Buddha] three times;
having reverently joined their palms and prostrated at the Buddha’s feet as an offering,
they all withdrew with dignified decorum and sat to one side.
At that time, Maitreya and the other great bodhisattvas,
seeing that the great assembly had all gathered like clouds,
formed this thought: "I observe that the entire assembly has come to the presence of the Buddha."
"He shall surely expound the inconceivable, sublime Dharma;
let everyone quiet their thoughts and wait with bated breath to hear his subtle words.
At that time, the World-Honored One knew the thoughts in the minds of all the bodhisattvas and the entire great assembly.
Immediately arising from samādhi, he addressed the Bodhisattva King Adorned, saying:
"Son of good family, you should now go and observe this great earth.
What do you see?"
Then, having received the Buddha’s instruction,
the Bodhisattva King Adorned rose from his seat, surveyed the great earth,
and having completed his survey, returned to the presence of the Buddha.
Having prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, he stood to one side and addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
I have followed the Buddha’s instruction and observed this great earth.”
All the great assemblies of devas and humans have gathered like clouds; we pray that, out of compassion, you will perform deeds for the benefit of all sentient beings.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva King Adorned, saying:

"You should listen with single-minded attention to what I shall say: I am now going to bestow the prophecy of unsurpassed bodhi upon six hundred and forty billion sentient beings who possess the karmic affinity.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi rose from his seat.
Joining his palms toward the Buddha, he addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"World-Honored One, there are now immeasurable billions of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and various rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and humans."
As well as non-humans and all those of external paths, have all gathered together;
now is the very time for the World-Honored One.
We only pray that you will preach the *Sarvadharma-guṇavyūharāja-sūtra*, which is able to dissolve all karmic obstructions.
It can extinguish all sins and sufferings,
sever all demonic activities,
and cause sentient beings who have not yet developed faith to give rise to reverent trust.
It eliminates famine so that there is constant abundance and joy;
it eradicates all diseases and keeps one far removed from untimely death;
and it causes sentient beings to forever eliminate regret.
They all attained peace and security, constantly experiencing happiness.
World-Honored One, in the past, I once heard this sutra from the Buddha Vidyutprabha.
As soon as I had heard it, all sublime dharmas became manifest before me.
"All evil realms are completely closed off, and all karmic obstructions are entirely eliminated.
We pray that, out of compassion, you will expound this for the sake of the assembly.
Having spoken these words, the World-Honored One remained silent.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi likewise earnestly entreated him three times to preach [the Dharma].
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Good son, do not request that I preach the *Sarvadharmaguṇavyūharāja Sūtra*.
Why is this? If I were to preach it, there will be sentient beings in the evil world of the future."
They are unable to believe or accept it, speaking thus:
"This sutra was not spoken by the Tathāgata," nor do they praise or disparage this sutra.
Although it is capable of bringing about both wholesome and unwholesome karma, those sentient beings, due to their stinginess and greed,
are unable to respect and make offerings to this sutra,
nor do they draw near to the Dharma-preacher.
By slandering this sutra and extensively giving rise to lack of faith,
they will create manifold evil karmas in the present life and fall into the hells in future lives to undergo the suffering of being scorched.
Good son, this king of sutras is deeply worthy of veneration, like one's own father and mother;
furthermore, it is able to extinguish all obstacles of evil karma.
However, in this world of the five turbidities, it is neither the time for such teaching nor the time for listening. Why is this?
Lest all those non-Buddhists and sentient beings [be led astray].
They fall into the realms of hell beings, hungry ghosts, and animals, where they undergo various sufferings for a long time.
Yet these sentient beings lack faith;
they are attached to various desires, diligently occupied with worldly affairs, trade, and litigation.
They will certainly give rise to a mind of slander toward this sutra.
After these beings pass away,
they shall fall into the eight great hells and undergo extreme suffering.
At that time, there were eighty thousand people in the assembly who all rose from their seats,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
and addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One!”
We, with our profound resolve, believe in this sutra;
we honor, make offerings to, transcribe, read, recite, and extensively explain it to others.
If there are foolish people who do not believe in this Dharma, [we shall protect them].
Because they are arrogant regarding the Dharma, they shall also revile and treat me with contempt;
at that time, I shall endure it all,
repaying the kindness of this sutra without ever harboring resentment or anger.
I only pray that you will preach this sublime sūtra. Why is this?
Because this king of sūtras will benefit sentient beings in future ages no differently than the Buddha himself.
Having spoken these words, he withdrew and sat to one side.
The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva seek a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra)?"
The Buddha said, "Good son,
one who seeks a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) should accomplish four dharmas in this way.
The first is to go frequently to inquire [of them]."
Second, the arousal of a mind of diligent effort;
third, purity of intention;
fourth, reverence and love for the Dharma.
The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha,
saying, "World-Honored One, how does a bodhisattva dwell in an araṇya?
The Buddha said, "Good son, by accomplishing four dharmas, a bodhisattva dwells in an araṇya."
First, to abandon the household life;
second, to distance oneself from evil associates;
third, to completely relinquish wealth and possessions.
"Fourth, one should always restrain one's own mind.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I do not see anyone who hears this sutra falling into the evil realms."
“World-Honored One, this sutra possesses great majestic power that is difficult to fathom.
World-Honored One, if anyone should even briefly hear this sutra, prostrate to it, praise it, make offerings to it, and revere it, they shall obtain immeasurable merit.”
How much more so for those who copy, read, recite, and uphold it;
who offer various kinds of incense and flowers as worship;
and who provide clothing, food, and other necessities as offerings to the Dharma teacher.
Such persons are protected and remembered by all Buddhas together;
they shall receive a prediction of enlightenment and will attain rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
"Such a Dharma-preacher is no different from the Buddha.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
I too shall make offerings to such a Dharma-preacher and grant him a prophecy [of enlightenment]."
They shall be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss and swiftly proceed toward Bodhi.
Furthermore, if there are those who, having shown respect and reverence toward the Buddhas and this sutra, [practice accordingly...]
Those who make offerings with exquisite fragrances, flowers, unguents, powdered incense,
garments, necklaces, and various kinds of music,
as well as banners, parasols, and silken streamers.
This person shall ultimately never suffer an untimely or violent death;
they shall have no fear of enemies, bandits, or military conflict;
nor shall they experience the suffering of grief for parents, wives, children, kinsmen, friends, or spiritual mentors.
Whatever they aspire to shall not fail to be fulfilled according to their wishes.
Good son, the appearance of the Buddhas in the world is an event of extreme rarity.
To hear this sutra is even more difficult than that.
Wherever this scripture may be— whether in cities, towns, villages, forest hermitages, or other dwellings— [it shall be honored].
"You should know that this stage is that which is sustained by all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, as for the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara..."
"For what reason is he named Avalokiteśvara?
The World-Honored One replied,
"Because he constantly observes all sentient beings in the world with his pure eyes."
By providing consolation, bringing beings to maturity, and acting with compassion for their benefit, one attains peace and security.
If anyone invokes his name, all their aspirations and requests shall be fulfilled.
For these reasons, he is named Avalokiteśvara.
He spoke again to the Buddha, saying:
"If there are sentient beings who merely invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
they shall still obtain the fulfillment of their sought-after aims."
How much more so for those who make offerings to the Tathāgata and this sutra—
copying it, reading and reciting it, and explaining it extensively for others—
and who offer robes, incense, and flowers as worship.
This person shall obtain immeasurable and boundless merit.
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, this sutra possesses great majestic power and is capable of performing the work of a Buddha."
"I only pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion for all sentient beings,
will further preach a dhāraṇī mantra for them.
The Buddha said, "Good son, there is a dhāraṇī."
It is named Victorious Sublime (Jinmiao).
In the past, when I was a bodhisattva,
I was at the place of the Buddha Wondrous Sound (Miaoyin) in the world Victorious Sublime.
Together with the great assembly, they heard this dhāraṇī mantra.
Having received it, they realized the dharma of the ten stages (daśabhūmi),
and immeasurable sentient beings all attained the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
At that time, the assembly of bodhisattvas rose from their seats and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, we pray only that you will look upon us with compassion and pity;
we shall now recite this dhāraṇī mantra."
At that time, the World-Honored One, with a Brahma-voice, spoke this mantra:

*Tadyathā | śye śye | śyā-vaho khava-ho | śyā-vaho | huru huru padma abhrama-vame sarasvati dṛdhe dṛdhe dṛdhara-dṛdhe devakule paripāriṇi yutodadhe prakarṣaṇi varṣaṇi bhagavan mama nāmam amukaḥ | by the protection of the Buddha, may all my aspirations be fulfilled; may all sinful karma be entirely eliminated. Svāhā.* The Buddha said: "Good son, this is a supreme and wondrous dhāraṇī-mantra."
It can eliminate all karmic obstacles and transgressions;
it can subjugate the armies of others;
and it ensures that there will forever be no occurrences of famine, pestilence, calamities, or the suffering of disease.
It can always ensure abundance such that granaries overflow and it increases one's lifespan.
This dharani mantra is the mother of all Buddhas.
If there are good sons or good daughters, [who recite it...]
With faith, they prostrate, pay homage, and make offerings;
they copy, read, recite, and uphold this sutra,
and likewise make offerings to the Dharma masters who uphold it.
This person’s karmic obstacles will all be extinguished, and they shall not meet with an untimely death.
In this very life, they will constantly experience joy and happiness,
while their parents, wife, children, friends, and kinsmen will all be secure and at peace.
All their aspirations and requests will be fulfilled without exception.
The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I too shall respectfully uphold this sutra."
Furthermore, if there should be anyone who offers exquisite incense, flowers,
and various foods and drinks to this sutra and its Dharma-preacher,
I too shall rejoice and offer my mind in worship to this sutra.
"In that land, I shall protect the king and all the people;
I shall cause them to be free from decline and affliction, and ensure that their every aspiration is fulfilled.
World-Honored One, I now rouse a heart of courageous vigor."
For the sake of that king and those who have faith and accept [the teaching],
I shall also proclaim a dhāraṇī mantra to provide protection for them.
The Buddha said, "Good son,"
"I shall rejoice in you being able to speak this dhāraṇī for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
through the empowerment of the Buddha’s spiritual power, [spoke].
He spoke this dhāraṇī mantra:
Namaḥ sarvabuddhatathāgatebhyaḥ. Namaḥ amitābhāya.
Tathāgatāya namaḥ sarvabodhisattvānāṃ namo sarvamārīcikebhyaḥ tadyathā hu me hu me.
Mati mahāmati vajramati tīkṣṇavajramati.
tathāgatānuparivartita sara sara
Āyurmukhi bhṛkuṭi vikurva mukhi.
Kṛṣṇe kṛṣṇa-rūpe kiṭi.

*Sādyanusmara bhagavan vajrapāṇe sarvabuddhakarmalaye*. [I, so-and-so—here one states one’s own name—whatever aspirations and desires I have, may they all be fulfilled according to my wishes. Grant me these vows through the true word of the Buddha, the true word of the Dharma, the true word of the Bodhisattvas, and the true word of the Śrāvakas. Svāhā! World-Honored One, if there are further persons who wish to enter the stages of a Bodhisattva, who desire to behold all the Tathāgatas, and who delight in being born in the Pure Lands...
Furthermore, those who desire wealth, nobility, abundant treasures, freedom from illness,
and long life should uphold this subtle and wondrous sutra as well as the Dharma Master,
by copying, reading, reciting, and honoring it with incense, flowers, music, and song.
They shall provide offerings of clothing, food and drink, silken canopies, banners, and streamers.
Such persons as these I shall protect; their aspirations shall be fulfilled, and I shall cherish them with affection as if they were my only son.
World-Honored One, if there should be anyone who, by nature dull-witted and ignorant, desires to seek intelligence,
or who wishes to protect a kingdom so that it may be free from pestilence,
they should begin on the eighth day of the waxing moon.
One day, one shall fast and recite this mantra,
continuing until the fifteenth day or even the end of the month;
during that time, one shall consume only the three kinds of white foods.
This refers to white cakes and milk curds.
Having purified oneself through bathing, one should recite this divine mantra one hundred thousand times.
If one has the capacity, one should recite it three hundred thousand times and always make offerings to the Triple Gem according to one's means.
Next, have the painter observe the eight precepts and fast;
with body and clothing pure and clean, he shall paint the image.
Within the studio, install an image of Śākyamuni Buddha.
Seated upon the lion throne, he performs the ritual of preaching the Dharma;
to his right is placed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
adorned with all manner of ornaments.
Standing upon a lotus flower, his body has four arms;
the upper right hand holds a Sanskrit manuscript,
and the lower right hand holds a rosary.
In the upper left hand he holds a white lotus,
and in the lower left hand he grasps a kundaṭīka staff;
to his left is stationed the deity Vajrapāṇi.
His right hand holds a vajra,
while his left hand reaches out from afar to support the head of the vajra.
His countenance is serene and joyful, and his body is adorned with necklaces and ornaments.
On its four sides, one should install the Four World-Protecting Heavenly Kings (Lokapālas).
All these honored images should have the Buddha’s relics contained within silk bands and inserted into their bodies.
Next, one should prepare an altar before the image, its size determined according to the occasion,
with doors opening on all four sides,
and smeared with cow dung.
Various kinds of incense and flowers were scattered upon it.
Five incense burners were set up separately, each burning one of the five types of incense:
namely, agallochum, sandalwood, storax, benzoin, and frankincense.
At each of the four gates of the maṇḍala, place two vases,
either filled with clear water or with milk.
Arrange sixteen lamp bowls in their respective locations.
Hang silk banners, canopies, and various musical instruments;
sprinkle the ground with scented water and offer worship with fragrant flowers, food, and drink.
At the four corners of the altar, have people recite this sutra.
Each person shall bathe and put on fresh, clean clothing, and eat the three white foods.
Place flowers in their hands and have them join their palms to state the matter for which they seek assistance.
Arousing a mind of loving-kindness and making aspirations according to your wishes, scatter flowers before the Buddha;
whatever you aspire for shall be fulfilled according to your heart.
Within seven days, I shall manifest a most excellent form for you.
May they cause [the practitioner] to see auspicious dreams and converse with them;
may they fulfill their aspirations and remove their lack of faith.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent!"
"You have been able to take pity on all sentient beings and speak this dhāraṇī method.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
This sublime sūtra is difficult to encounter;
sentient beings of meager merit,
though this sūtra exists within their own country, are unable to see it.
Furthermore, they will be unable to write it down, read it, recite it, hear it, or uphold it.
Why is this? It is because evil Māras create obstacles.
Moreover, son of good family, if there are sentient beings...
When one copies, reads, or recites this sutra,
four evil māras will cause disturbances and confusion.
What are these four?
First, the arising of indolence;
second, the giving rise to a lack of faith;
third, the failure to show respect toward the Dharma teacher.
Fourth, the mind cannot become concentrated.
This person should recognize that this is the work of Māra.
Furthermore, there are four kinds of evil deeds of Māra.
What are the four?
First, distancing oneself from virtuous friends;
second, improper mental attention.
Third, they do not understand written characters.
Fourth, they perceive only the present and claim there is no future;
they commit various evil deeds without fear in their hearts and preach that there is no cause and effect.
What I have taught is that all else is not the Dharma;
those who delight in worldly affairs and are entangled by greedy attachments—
such sentient beings shall fall into hell.
They undergo great suffering and affliction for incalculable eons.
Furthermore, there are four kinds of māras; what are these four?
First is attachment to wealth and possessions.
Second, associating with evil friends;
third, creating obstacles for the Dharma Master;
fourth, recounting the Master’s faults and transgressions when he preaches the Dharma.
Due to these karmic actions, these sentient beings shall suffer poverty;
they will not encounter virtuous friends and will remain far removed from honored teachers.
They will conceive false views, asserting that there is no cause and no effect.
They shall fall into hell and undergo all manner of agonizing sufferings.
The Buddha addressed the great assembly: "I now tell you this true word for a second and third time:
do not be negligent, and do not treat this sutra with contempt."
Believe and accept this with a single mind; do not give rise to slander.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke these verses:
I have previously proclaimed the kings of all sutras, enabling all sentient beings to attain perfect enlightenment;
now I further proclaim this truly wondrous scripture.
Hearing it, you should practice with reverence so as not to undergo the extreme sufferings of the future, falling into the hells for many kalpas.
Those who can give rise to faith in this sutra will, in every lifetime,
always be my true children; furthermore, those who make offerings to this sutra shall be born in the Pure Land,
where no rākṣasas or ghosts and spirits shall deceive them, nor shall any evils come to invade or disturb them.
Wherever this King of Sūtras resides, there shall be no calamities capable of harming anyone;
all their aspirations shall be fulfilled according to their hearts' desire, and they shall dwell in peace until reaching the shore of Bodhi.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings, having heard these verses, [rejoiced].
Weeping with tears flowing and his entire body trembling,
he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and said, “World-Honored One,
if we, the Four Heavenly Kings, should see a Dharma teacher who upholds this sutra...”
When he preaches this Dharma, I shall make offerings to him,
and I shall provide protection for all those who listen.
If there should be a king regarding this sutra...
To those who write, read, recite, uphold, and make offerings [to this],
I shall provide protection and regard the people of that land as my only son;
I shall also supply them with clothing and necklaces.
May that kingdom’s borders abound in wealth and treasures, lacking nothing;
may it always achieve victory in times of war.
Mindful of repaying the Buddha’s kindness, I shall remain free from indolence.
Blessed One, if there should be anyone who, upon hearing this sutra,
does not give rise to faith and fails to make offerings to the Dharma-preacher,
I have no skillful means to deal with such a person.
"Though you are able to rescue and liberate others, you have merely given rise to anxiety and distress.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent! You protect the True Dharma;
you are able to give rise to such a heart of profound reverence."
At that time, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Heavenly King and Lord of the Gandharvas,
rose from his seat, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
and with palms joined in reverence, addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One, ...”
In future ages, there will be sentient beings who constantly practice unwholesome deeds and do not believe in the Tathāgata;
they will be unable to make offerings to, transcribe, read, or recite this sutra.
Furthermore, they do not practice giving, nor do they believe that there is a reward of happiness in the present life for the act of giving.
Out of great compassion, the World-Honored One has preached this sutra for the sake of such unbelievers,
so that they may receive and practice it.
The Buddha said, "Good son, there are two things that cause all sentient beings to fall into the great hells and transmigrate through the cycle of birth and death:
first, sexual desire; second, anger."
Furthermore, there are four dharmas that cause sentient beings to be born among humans and devas. What are the four?
First, maintaining a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings.
Second, giving rise to a mind of profound reverence toward the Triple Gem.
Third, they are able to give away all their means of livelihood.
Fourth, they firmly maintain the pure conduct (brahmacarya) without any deficiency.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, [spoke as follows].
And he spoke in verse:
Generosity possesses great majestic power; It uproots the suffering of sentient beings within the three evil realms.
Deluded by stinginess, greed, and ignorance, Their minds are tormented by various defiled desires.
Those who hear this sutra yet do not respectfully accept it, lacking faith and generosity within the Buddha-dharma,
shall fall into the evil realms and undergo boundless, great suffering. To benefit the sovereign and the people,
I have preached this sutra, which is endowed with majestic power and virtue.
It causes one to be free from malignant diseases and various demonic afflictions, and prevents harm from yakṣas and the like.
For those who have faith and transcribe this sūtra, making offerings to it can generate immeasurable merit.
Even if all sentient beings possessed wisdom equal to that of a Buddha, they could not exhaustively describe its merit throughout many kalpas.
If one were to spend many eons making offerings to all the Bodhisattvas,
it would not equal the merit of writing even a single character from this sublime King of Sutras with a momentary heart of faith;
compared to this latter merit, the former virtue does not approach even a hundred-millionth part.
Therefore, the wise person should single-mindedly practice this sutra without indolence.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
In a future age, if there are sons or daughters of good family who develop deep reverence and faith in this sutra,
and [offer] exquisite incense, flowers, various foods and drinks, clothing, and bedding;
One should offer worship to all those who preach this Dharma,
as well as to those who copy, read, and recite this sutra;
such a person will certainly obtain immeasurable merit and benefit in this present life.
Their bodies will be benefited and freed from all suffering of illness;
their six sense organs, such as the eyes, will be pure and free from affliction;
and they shall not encounter calamities such as water, fire, or famine.
Furthermore, they shall not be harmed by malignant poisons;
all sentient beings who see them will rejoice.
At the time of their death, they will see the Buddha Akṣobhya coming to console and encourage them.
He addressed him, saying: "O son of good family, the roots of virtue you have cultivated are of immeasurable merit.
You may take birth in any pure land throughout the ten directions, including the world of Ultimate Bliss, according to your wish.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara—
He addressed the Buddha, saying, “Excellent, excellent, World-Honored One!
Out of compassion for the sentient beings within Jambudvīpa, you have spoken this sutra.
In future ages, it shall extensively perform the work of a Buddha to benefit sentient beings.”
This great vidyā-mantra can eliminate all extremely heavy karmic obstructions.
The Buddha said, "Good son,
sentient beings with evil karma possess sins that are profound and grave."
If one has not heard this sutra, one cannot transcribe, receive, uphold, read, or recite it.
If there are sentient beings who hear this scripture,
they shall transcribe, receive, uphold, respect, and make offerings to it.
One should know that all this is due to the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who can explain even a single word of this sutra for the sake of others, [the merit is immeasurable].
To make offerings to this person is no different from making offerings to the Buddha.
Why is this, son of good family?
This sutra was proclaimed by seven thousand Buddhas of the past.
All bodhisattvas universally rejoice;
the devas protect the mother of this bodhisattva.
At that time, the Vajradhara Bodhisattva...
He addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One, in future ages,
where shall this sutra be fully circulated?"
The Buddha said, "Good son,
this sutra shall exist in its entirety within the palace of the Sea Dragon King and among the Trāyastriṃśa devas;
in Jambudvīpa, it shall circulate in small portions wherever it may be."
The Buddha said, "Good son,
I now entrust this sutra to you. You should receive,
uphold, make offerings to, and protect it, no differently than you would the Buddha."
Circulate it in all places so that it shall never be interrupted;
benefit sentient beings and extensively perform the Buddha-work.
The Vajradhara Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, I now accept the Buddha’s instruction to propagate this sutra,
and I shall likewise protect those Dharma-preachers who uphold it.
The Buddha said, “Excellent, excellent, son of good family!”
"This is indeed the work you have performed.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,"
I now reverently prostrate with utmost sincerity to such a subtle and wondrous sūtra,
and I shall make offerings to all who preach it and those who transcribe it.
World-Honored One, if there should be a land of meager merit ruled by an unrighteous king, [may this sūtra prevail].
If there is this sutra but it cannot be honored,
and the Dharma master is likewise not honored, this sutra will disappear;
then calamities, misfortunes, and disasters shall manifest before that land.
In this way, you should know that the True Dharma is about to perish.
When the wise see this, they should make offerings with a sincere heart.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent, son of good family! It is just as you have said."
Suppose there were someone who, for a full thousand years,
provided all manner of articles of pleasure as offerings to great bodhisattvas and śrāvakas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
Furthermore, if one were to give as alms treasures of the seven jewels equal in number to these grains of sand, and subsequently sacrifice one's own body—
good son, such merit compared to the merit of making offerings to those who uphold this sutra [is infinitesimal].
Even a single phrase or a single word of this [sūtra] exceeds it by a hundred thousand millionfold;
how much more so if one can write it out in its entirety and recite it?
Why is this? Because this sūtra and these mantras possess great majestic power.
If one upholds this, they will realize that the body is devoid of solidity;
seeing all phenomena as like illusions and dreams, they will know the selflessness of dharmas.
Having received the Buddha’s prediction of enlightenment, they shall attain great bodhi.
At that time, the entire assembly of bodhisattvas,
as well as the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, humans, non-humans, and others,
all with one mind and in unison, praised the Buddha, saying, "Excellent, excellent!"
This is the second turning of the Great Wheel of Dharma.
We shall all reverently honor and make offerings to it.
In whatever country, territory, city, or town this sutra may reside—
I shall likewise provide protection for both [the assembly] and the preachers of this Dharma.
If there are sentient beings who slander this sutra,
they shall incur immeasurable heavy offenses in their present bodies.
"After their lives end, they shall fall into hell;
I shall abandon such persons and will not provide them with protection.
The Buddha said, "Good son," [he continued].
I now likewise entrust this sūtra to you.
In future ages, you shall propagate it widely so that it does not perish.
This sūtra possesses great benefit and brings peace and happiness to humans and devas alike.
This increases one's field of merit and brings liberation from the three evil realms.
Do not give rise to doubt, but always encourage others to receive and uphold it.
When the Buddha spoke this sutra, [the assembly rejoiced].
Sixty-four thousand people all attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). Then,
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who,
with faith, copy, receive, uphold, read, recite, and make offerings to this sutra,
where will such persons be reborn at the end of their lives, and how much merit will they obtain?”
The Buddha said, "Good son,
because you are able to ask about this matter of supreme merit,
when this person's life ends, they will forever leave the evil realms and always be born in a pure land."
Even if someone were to practice the bodhisattva path by giving away their head,
eyes, hands, feet, as well as their wife and children,
it would still not be equal to upholding this sutra.
"Wherever this sutra may be located,
that place shall be as a stupa and should be honored with offerings.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva then addressed the Buddha again, saying:
World-Honored One, in future ages, I shall bestow a prediction of enlightenment upon those who uphold this sutra;
they shall extinguish the extremely heavy karmic obstacles of the five heinous crimes.
For ninety thousand kalpas he shall constantly enjoy wealth and nobility;
for eighty thousand kalpas he shall act as a wheel-turning sage king (cakravartin).
The Buddha said, "So it is, so it is, son of good family."
I recall that in the past, immeasurable kalpas ago,
there was a Buddha, a World-Honored One named Anantaguṇadharmajñānaviśuddhatārārāja Tathāgata.
At that time, I was a brahmin.
Having heard this sutra from that Buddha,
they received, upheld, read, and recited it, thereby attaining the purity of the Dharma-eye.
Those who heard it together with them have, from that time forward, never fallen into the evil realms.
Gradually, you shall attain unsurpassed bodhi.
Son of good family, throughout immeasurable and vast kalpas,
for the sake of this Dharma, I have relinquished all wealth and treasures.
"Even at the cost of head, eyes, hands, feet, wife, children, and city-states,
you should practice the pure brahma-faring with a mind free from regret or affliction;
you all should likewise cultivate yourselves in this way."
At that time, the great assembly, having heard the account of his past ascetic practices,
all wept and said to the Buddha:
"It is rare, World-Honored One, that in future ages..."
Those who are able to receive, uphold, read, recite, and make offerings to this sutra shall obtain immeasurable merit.
This applies whether they be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās.
They are unable to recite this king of sutras;
they are unwilling to accept and uphold the dharani mantras;
nor are they able to diligently cultivate the six perfections.
Those who lack compassion for those in suffering will,
for immeasurable eons, fall into the ocean of birth and death and undergo all manner of afflictions.
Good son, it is like a woman who is heavily pregnant for ten months;
at that time, this woman suffers from various ailments,
her limbs ache as if being cut by knives, and she is unable to eat or drink.
At the time of childbirth, one undergoes great and intense suffering and thinks:
"If I am spared from this calamity, I shall never again engage in sexual desire and will always practice the holy life (brahmacarya).
Yet, as soon as the birth has occurred, one returns to practicing unwholesome ways.
They then forget the suffering and distress they previously endured.
Good son, in future ages, foolish sentient beings will be just like this:
they will not believe in this sutra, nor will they read, recite, practice giving, uphold the precepts, exercise patience, exert diligence, cultivate meditative concentration, or develop wisdom.
Clinging greedily to worldly sentiments,
they delight in mundane affairs and do not practice the causes for the purity of the three karmas;
such sentient beings only give rise to a mind of regret after they have already fallen into hell.
Just as a pregnant woman experiences extreme suffering, so too,
after undergoing such torment and emerging from hell,
one obtains a human body and becomes addicted to the pleasures of the five desires.
The sufferings of those hells cannot be remembered, yet they continue to create evil karma.
Good son, it is like a person who drinks much medicinal wine;
having drunk it, he becomes so dazed that he does not know his own home.
Having never recollected the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, nor his parents, wife, or children,
and being devoid of any sense of reverence due to his state of intoxication, he eventually went to the dangerous place of the charnel ground.
Furthermore, he was without any sense of fear or trepidation,
thinking to himself:
"How could any among the devas, nāgas, or yakṣas possibly frighten me?"
Thus, although such a drunken person may lie prostrate among thorns at that time and conceive the notion of pleasure,
once the intoxication has worn off, he will surely harbor distress and remorse.
Knowing for oneself that this was contrary to the Dharma, one resolves:
"From this day forth until the end of my life, I shall no longer drink alcohol or commit various transgressions.
Yet later, encountering adverse conditions, one returns to indulging in drink and once again commits faults as before.
Ignorant sentient beings are just like this:
because of their defiled craving, they accumulate great wealth and indulge in various forms of arrogance and negligence,
failing to keep the Triple Gem in mind.
Having abandoned and turned their backs on their honored parents, they likewise do not practice generosity, ethical discipline, patience, and so forth;
nor do they desire to seek a pure buddha-field.
Such sentient beings constantly dwell within the shoreless ocean of birth and death.
One shall fall into hell and undergo manifold sufferings for a long time.
Even if one should obtain a human birth, at the time of dwelling in the womb,
one will experience various afflictions and have the body oppressed by suffering.
He then thought to himself: "If I am able to escape this calamity, I shall never again commit transgressions that lead to such extreme suffering.
I will constantly cultivate wholesome deeds and vow to be reborn in a Pure Land."
Having obtained this human body, because of ignorance you have committed various sinful deeds and will fall back into the evil realms.
Therefore, you all should practice well and not be negligent; this is my brief instruction and admonition.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, what is the name of this sutra, and how should it be upheld?
The Buddha said: "This sutra has five names in total."
First, it is titled "Saving All Sentient Beings from Suffering and Calamity";
second, "The True Inquiry of the Bodhisattva";
and third, "The King Adorned with Supernatural Powers."
The fourth is named Able to Accomplish the Perfect Enlightenment of All Buddhas;
the fifth is named King Adorned with the Merits of All Dharmas.
After the Buddha had spoken this sutra, he said:
The great bodhisattvas and the assembly of śrāvakas, as well as the devas,
nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, gandharvas, humans, non-humans, and others,
were all greatly rejoiced, and they faithfully accepted and practiced it.

The *Buddhabhāṣita-sarvaguṇavyūharāja-sūtra*, translated by order of the Emperor by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing at Dafuxian Monastery in Luozhou on the fifteenth day of the seventh month of the first year of the Shénlóng era of the Great Táng.

The text was compiled and the characters corrected by the śramaṇa and brahmacārin Paṇḍita Dàdù, who read the Sanskrit original, while the śramaṇas and brahmacārin translators rendered it into Chinese.

At the Longxing Monastery in Jingzhou of the Great Tang, the *śramaṇa* Mahāsaṃghika Upādhyāya Hongjing, the *śramaṇa* Mahāsaṃghika Upādhyāya Dazhi, the *śramaṇa* Mahāsaṃghika Upādhyāya Shengzhuang, and the *śramaṇa* Xuansan of Chanhe Monastery in Xiangzhou served as proofreaders and scribes for the translation of the scriptures.
The *śramaṇa* Mahāsaṃghika Upādhyāya Dazhi of the Dazongchi Monastery served as the chief proofreader for the translation of the scriptures.

The *śramaṇa* Mahāsaṃghika Upādhyāya Shengzhuang of the Dajianfu Monastery served as the verifier of the meaning for the translation of the scriptures. The *śramaṇa* Xuansan of Chanhe Monastery in Xiangzhou received the dictation for the translation of the scriptures.
